To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Ishikawa cells are a suitable model for the study of steroid hormone receptors and that the regulation of both ER and PR levels in Ishikawa cells can be demonstrated by using monoclonals.
the human endometrial cancer cell line Ishikawa expresses both estrogen and progsterone receptors, and that the levels of both types of receptors are under hormonal regulation.

the Ishikawa cell line is useful for studying the regulation of both estrogen receptor (ER) and progesterone (PR) levels in human endocarcinoma, and that estradiol increases the PR levels and R5020 decreases the ER levels in the Ishikawa cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a simple and rapid method of immunocytochemical detection of estrogen and progsterone receptor content in Ishikawa cells, a human endometrial cell line.
a new approach to the immunocytochemical analysis of the regulation of estrogen and progsterone receptor levels in a human endometrial cell line.

a quantitative immunocytochemical study of ER and PR levels in Ishikawa cells, and the effect of estradiols and progestins on ER and PR levels, which may provide a useful tool for the study of the mechanisms of action of these steroids in human endometrium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Ishikawa cells express estrogen and progesteron receptors in the nuclei, that both receptors show intercellular heterogeneity in content, that the level of estrogen receptor can be regulated in the cells by progesterone and that the level of progesterone receptor can be regulated by estrogens.

the immunocytochemical assay is a useful tool for monitoring estrogen and progesteron receptor levels in Ishikawa cells, which can be used as a model for the study of the regulation of these receptors in normal and neoplastic endometrial tissue.

the Ishikawa cell line is a useful model for studying the hormonal regulation of estrogen and progosterone receptor expression in human endometrium and for investigating the mechanisms of action of steroid hormones in endometrial cancer cells.
